source_refs.note: Topic 16.2.2 with Figure 16.2 (pictograms), printed page 338. The pictograms themselves are not reproduced.

blocks.text: A laboratory worker must use chemicals according to the standard procedures, keeping in view the particular hazards and the precautions required for their safe use. The print shows the pictograms of chemical hazards as Figure 16.2; the hazard pictograms on a reagent label tell the worker which precautions a chemical needs.

blocks.alt: Nine red-bordered diamond pictograms with simple black symbols: explosive (a bursting bomb), flammable (a flame), oxidising (a flame over a circle), compressed gas (a gas cylinder), corrosive (liquid dripping from tubes onto a surface and a hand), toxic (a skull and crossbones), irritant or harmful (an exclamation mark), harmful to the environment (a dead tree and fish) and health hazard (a person with a star-shaped mark on the chest).
blocks.caption: Pictograms of chemical hazards (original diagram after Figure 16.2).
Chemical hazards in practice
rows: Follow the standard procedure for each chemical
Never taste or smell a compound or gas

blocks.prompt: Before using a reagent for the first time, where does a student find its particular hazards?
blocks.explanation: In the standard procedure for the chemical and on the hazard pictograms on its label; the student identifies these hazards and the required precautions before beginning the work.

items: Chemical hazards: use every chemical by its standard procedure, knowing its particular hazards and precautions (hazard pictograms, Figure 16.2).
